used.how: the copy's added time is taken in one profiler window behind 100 matmuls, stock and exact calls alternating (no host-dispatch wait in a single op's device time)
the receivers' deadline is the light chips' own work at the DRAM floor (0.467 ms); the measured copy times are fed to P.55a's model against it
a whole slot in one call is known to cost when it competes with rows, so rows keep priority (copy pieces only in idle rounds under a cap) and the cost is measured, not assumed hidden

missing: the fabric's per-link rate for one worker sender (~15 GB/s at 10880 B packets; expert_slot_copy's 0.71 ms used both links, which P.55a's '2 paths' lever read as one link pair a path)
2D fabric multicast writes one address on every chip of a rectangle, so it cannot drop a replica off at chosen chips without clobbering the others' spare slots

overseer.evidence: nothing padded or duplicated; the kernel was extended (REC_FX) instead

no Python-built op added or touched: routed_experts_combine is a C++ device op with its program cache (REC_FX hashed in fill_exact); the exact jobs are a DRAM tensor read by the kernel, the args are patched per call by set_combine_fill_args
no fork regression suite run on the 8x4; only the new test (gate unit P.55b) and the gate's determinism unit

(1) per-block ready flags every 32 pieces with arrival stamps (first block 0.04-0.07 ms), relays gated on them; receiver compute on landed blocks left to P.55c; (2) every copy on both links of the hop (0.89 ms vs 1.40 on one), and a 4-link detour through a free chip (0.76 ms); (3) the home re-reads the slot from DRAM (one extra 19.9 MB read an edge, inside the added time: pair +0.11 ms, 4 links +0.01); copies on time with P.55a's model: novel 0 of 174 (5.87 ms a chunk) / 0 of 269 (8.74) at 2 / 4 links, code 0 of 41 (1.25) / 0 of 74 (2.44); results/P.55b_exact_copy.json
